stories.headline: US and Iran trade fresh strikes across the Gulf as Hormuz truce collapses

key_facts.fact: Iran's army said on July 9 it attacked US military infrastructure in the Gulf, hitting US Patriot systems in Kuwait, an early-warning site in Qatar and a US Army fuel depot in Bahrain, in retaliation for US strikes a day earlier on about 90 Iranian military sites.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's army said in a statement released by state media that it had launched attacks on US Patriot systems in Kuwait, an early-warning site in Qatar and a US Army fuel depot in Bahrain.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they also fired 10 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Azraq military base, used by US forces, and at a US military command center in the region.
key_facts.excerpt: The Revolutionary Guards later said Iran had fired 10 ballistic missiles at Jordan's Azraq military base, which is used by US forces, and also a US military control center in the Middle East.

key_facts.fact: In Kuwait, falling debris wounded one person as the country shot down three ballistic missiles, a cruise missile and 10 drones; Jordan said all incoming Iranian fire was intercepted.
key_facts.excerpt: In Kuwait, the military said falling debris wounded one person as the nation shot down three ballistic missiles, a cruise missile and 10 drones.

key_facts.fact: Iran said at least 14 people were killed in US airstrikes over two days, including at least one member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran launched more missiles at U.S. allies Thursday and said at least 14 people were killed in U.S. airstrikes over the last two days.

key_facts.fact: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency kept the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of global oil passed before the war, at its highest level.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency says the security threat in the Strait of Hormuz remains at its highest level.

key_facts.fact: By July 10 a US official said there had been no fresh strikes on Iran in recent hours and that 'technical talks' between the two sides were continuing, with Washington still committed to a diplomatic resolution.
key_facts.excerpt: The United States has not carried out any fresh strikes on Iran in recent hours and remains committed to pursuing a diplomatic resolution, with 'technical talks' between the two sides continuing despite the latest escalation.

key_facts.fact: Israel's Defense Minister Israel Katz warned Israel was prepared to resume its military campaign against Iran if needed, vowing to do so 'with even greater force.'
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz has said his country was prepared to resume its military campaign against Iran if needed, vowing to do so 'with even greater force.'

stories.headline: Ukraine's drone campaign sets Russian tankers ablaze, deepening a national fuel crisis

key_facts.fact: On Thursday, July 9, Ukrainian drones struck more Russian oil facilities and set two oil tankers ablaze in the Sea of Azov.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian drones hit more Russian oil facilities and set two oil tankers ablaze in the Sea of Azov on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert 'Madyar' Brovdi reported on July 9 that long-range drones had struck 35 tankers, cargo ships and 'special vessels' in the Sea of Azov over three nights.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the course of three nights, Ukrainian long-range drones struck 35 tankers, cargo ships, and 'special vessels' in the Sea of Azov, Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces Commander Robert Brovdi, known by the callsign 'Madyar,' reported on July 9.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's drone force said at least 25 ships had been hit and set on fire over four days in the Sea of Azov, a clear blow to Russia's naval logistics and its fuel supply to occupied Crimea.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's drone force commander Robert Brovdi, also known as Magyar, says at least 25 ships have been hit and set on fire over the past four days in the Sea of Azov.

key_facts.fact: President Zelenskyy said forces also hit fuel infrastructure deep inside Russia, including an oil-pumping station in Ufa nearly 1,500 km from the border, calling the strikes part of a campaign of 'long-range sanctions.'
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy said his defence forces also hit a reserve fuel storage facility about 800km from the front line, and an oil-pumping station in Ufa nearly 1,500km from Ukraine's border... described the strikes as part of Kyiv's campaign of 'long-range sanctions.'

key_facts.fact: Drone strikes triggered a fire at an oil depot in Tver and set oil reservoirs ablaze in the Stavropol region, forcing the evacuation of several apartment buildings.
key_facts.excerpt: A Ukrainian drone strike triggered a fire at an oil depot in the western Russian city of Tver... Oil reservoirs also were set ablaze by drones in Vyazniki, in the southern Stavropol region... forcing the evacuation of several apartment buildings near the facility.

key_facts.fact: The strikes have caused a widespread fuel crisis in Russia with gasoline shortages and rationing, prompting President Putin to call on his government to subsidize fuel for people in occupied Crimea.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin has called on his government to provide subsidies for people living in Russian-occupied Crimea as fuel prices continue to soar amid Ukraine's ongoing campaign to cut off logistics to the peninsula.

stories.headline: EU says Meta's 'addictive' Instagram and Facebook design breaches Digital Services Act

key_facts.fact: On July 10 the European Commission preliminarily found Meta in breach of the Digital Services Act over the addictive design of Instagram and Facebook.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Commission has preliminarily found Meta in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) over the addictive design of Instagram and Facebook.

key_facts.fact: The finding centers on features including infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications and highly personalized recommendation algorithms that regulators say shift users into 'autopilot mode' and fuel compulsive use.
key_facts.excerpt: features including infinite scroll, autoplay, push notifications and highly personalised recommendation algorithms — tools regulators say shift users into 'autopilot mode' and fuel compulsive use.

key_facts.fact: The Commission called for structural changes: disabling autoplay and infinite scroll by default, introducing effective screen-time breaks and making recommendation systems less engagement-driven.
key_facts.excerpt: disabling features such as autoplay and infinite scroll by default, introducing effective screen-time breaks and adjusting its recommendation systems to make them less engagement-driven.

key_facts.fact: If the findings are confirmed, Meta faces a fine capped at 6% of its worldwide annual turnover, which could exceed $12 billion (about 11 billion euros) based on its 2025 revenue of just under $201 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta faces a fine capped at 6% of its total worldwide annual turnover — a figure that could run to more than $12 billion (€11bn) based on the company's 2025 revenue of just under $201 billion.

key_facts.fact: The investigation was launched in May 2024 and runs alongside a separate probe into Meta's age-assurance measures for under-13s; Meta can review the files and respond before any final non-compliance decision.
key_facts.excerpt: The Commission's investigation, launched in May 2024... The preliminary findings do not prejudge a final outcome. Meta now has the right to examine the Commission's investigation files and respond in writing before any non-compliance decision is issued.

stories.headline: Trump fires remaining Election Assistance Commission members ahead of midterms

key_facts.fact: On Thursday, July 9, President Trump fired the two Democratic members of the Election Assistance Commission, Thomas Hicks and Benjamin Hovland, via an email from the White House Presidential Personnel Office declaring their positions 'terminated, effective immediately.'
key_facts.excerpt: the other two Democratic appointees were fired via an email from the White House Presidential Personnel Office... 'your position as Commissioner of the Election Assistance Commission is terminated, effective immediately.'

key_facts.fact: The removals leave the four-member bipartisan commission without the three commissioners it needs to approve any action, eliminating its ability to help local officials prepare for the 2026 midterms.
key_facts.excerpt: eliminating the panel's ability to help local election officials prepare for the 2026 midterms... To approve any actions, the commission needs agreement from three of its four commissioners.

key_facts.fact: The White House cited a June 29 US Supreme Court decision granting the president broader power over the leadership of agencies Congress designed to be independent.
key_facts.excerpt: Commissioners were concerned after the June 29 U.S. Supreme Court decision granting Trump broad power over the leadership of agencies Congress designed to be independent.

key_facts.fact: The commission, created by the 2002 Help America Vote Act, is required to be evenly split between two Democrats and two Republicans, and all the ousted commissioners had been unanimously confirmed by the Senate.
key_facts.excerpt: The three remaining commissioners who were forced out, Thomas Hicks, Benjamin Hovland, and Christy McCormick, were all unanimously confirmed by the Senate... required to be evenly split with two Democrats and two Republicans.

key_facts.fact: The firings follow Trump's push for more federal intervention in voting, traditionally the responsibility of the states, as the November midterm elections approach.
key_facts.excerpt: a push by Trump for more federal intervention in voting processes, traditionally the purview of the states, as midterm elections approach in November.

stories.headline: US stocks rise and oil slides as jobless claims point to a still-steady labor market

key_facts.fact: US stocks closed higher on Thursday, July 9, despite renewed US-Iran strikes: the S&P 500 rose 0.81% to 7,543.65, the Nasdaq gained 1.30% to 26,206.89 and the Dow added 0.27% to 52,487.41 as easing oil prices supported sentiment.
key_facts.excerpt: The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 139.02 points, or 0.27%, to finish at 52,487.41. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1.30% to close at 26,206.89, while the S&P 500 rose 0.81% to 7,543.65.

key_facts.fact: Oil fell more than 2% on Thursday on worries that inflation and a slowing economy could weigh on demand, even as the US-Iran conflict limited supply: Brent dropped $1.92 (2.5%) to $76.10 and WTI fell $1.61 (2.2%) to $71.91.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures fell $1.92, or 2.5%, to $76.10 a barrel at 1:26 p.m. EDT... U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude fell $1.61, or 2.2%, to $71.91.

key_facts.fact: US initial jobless claims fell to 215,000 for the week ending July 4, below the 218,000 consensus and down from 217,000 the prior week, signaling a still-stable labor market.
key_facts.excerpt: the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance shrank to 215K for the week ending July 4. The latest print came in below initial estimates (218K) and was slightly lower than the previous week's 217K.

key_facts.fact: US existing home sales fell 2.4% in June to a 4.09 million annualized rate, well below the 4.20 million expected, as house prices hit a record.
key_facts.excerpt: US existing home sales fell 2.4% to 4.09m in June, down from 4.19m the month before and well below the 4.20m expected by the market.

key_facts.fact: Traders raised the implied probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike by December to about 87% after Wednesday's Fed minutes showed growing inflation concern.
key_facts.excerpt: Markets have increased the implied probability of a [hike] to about 87%.

stories.headline: GSK partner Hansoh reports first Phase III survival win for a B7-H3 cancer drug

key_facts.fact: On July 10, GSK's licensor Hansoh Pharma said its pivotal Phase III ARTEMIS-008 trial of risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) in advanced or relapsed small-cell lung cancer patients in China met its primary endpoint of overall survival versus standard-of-care topotecan.
key_facts.excerpt: ARTEMIS-008... met its primary endpoint of overall survival (OS). In the trial, conducted in patients in China, Ris-Rez demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in OS compared with the standard of care, topotecan.

key_facts.fact: The results are the first positive Phase III overall-survival data reported for a B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) in any tumor type.
key_facts.excerpt: These are the first positive phase III overall survival data reported for a B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) in any tumour type.

key_facts.fact: Benefit was consistent across secondary endpoints including progression-free survival, with no new safety signals; the data will support a regulatory submission in China.
key_facts.excerpt: Consistent benefit was also observed across key secondary endpoints, including progression-free survival... These data will be used by Hansoh Pharma for regulatory submission in China.

key_facts.fact: GSK holds exclusive rights to develop Ris-Rez outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan, and is running the global Phase III EMBOLD SCLC-301 trial, with pivotal data expected next year.
key_facts.excerpt: GSK holds exclusive global rights to develop Ris-Rez outside mainland China... GSK's broad clinical development programme includes... the global phase III EMBOLD SCLC-301 trial... with pivotal data expected next year.
